issue_context.title: Check Configuration Passes - Errors in syntax still reports - MQTT new Config issues
issue_context.body:
### The problem

With the new MQTT config (which I still don't understand why the huge breaking changes were needed, but ok, lets move on).
I spent an hour or two moving everything to the new syntax. Using "Check Configuration" from the Developer Tools area, I got an "Configuration Valid!", so I restart.

I then get numerus errors of:
```
 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.config] Invalid config for [sensor]: required key not provided @ data['state_topic']. Got None. (See /config/configuration.yaml, line 151).
```

Two Issues:

1. Line number is not helpful at all, its referencing my include.  So which sensor is it?  I have dozens.  Also, checking all of the `state_topics`, are valid and existing (and worked fine under the old mqtt syntax/layout just fine).

2. Passing "Check Configuration" when in fact it doesn't!

The Solution:

`state_topic` for MQTT anyways, now appears to require this syntax:
```
- state_topic: "mystate/topic/path"
```

when this used to work fine (what some of my sensors had)
```
- state_topic: mystate/topic/path
```

Please either fix the MQTT system, or have "Check Configuration" also require `"` for state_topics.  It would also be great if the logs spit out the line the caused the error.


### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.6.6

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2022.5.x

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

MQTT

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/mqtt/

### Diagnostics information

none

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
see above
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
see above
```


### Additional information

see above

<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

@marc-gist OK, so you're reporting 3 unrelated issues:
1. Line numbers in error messages do not work / are not helpful for `!include`
2. The "Check Configuration" button does not detect MQTT configuration errors
3. There's some issue with MQTT configuration where you now have to quote topics but it was previously not needed

1)
I'd suggest you open a separate issue about 1), tag it with integration `core` and ping me from it.

2)
I can reproduce the problem, let's get that fixed 👍 
Example config which doesn't make "Check Configuration" complain:
```
mqtt:                                
  sensor:                            
      some_illegal_topic: mystate/topic/path
```

3)
For 3), can you please come up with a concrete example where quoting topic strings is needed with the new MQTT configuration format but not with the old one?

Using the example from the issue description works fine:
```yaml
mqtt:
  sensor:
    - state_topic: mystate/topic/path
```

This worked pre 2022.6

```
sensor:
  - platform: mqtt
    name: "Barn Entrance Button Clicks"
    state_topic: iot/espToggleSwitchBarn/click
    unit_of_measurement: "click"
    icon: mdi:radiobox-marked
    availability_topic: "iot/espToggleSwitchBarn/LWT"
    
  - platform: mqtt
    name: "Barn Entrance Button Signal"
    state_topic: iot/espToggleSwitchBarn/status
    unit_of_measurement: "dB"
    device_class: signal_strength
    availability_topic: "iot/espToggleSwitchBarn/LWT"
    icon: mdi:router-wireless
```

changed to:
```
mqtt:
  sensor:
      - name: "Barn Entrance Button Clicks"
        state_topic: iot/espToggleSwitchBarn/click
        unit_of_measurement: "click"
        icon: mdi:radiobox-marked
        availability_topic: "iot/espToggleSwitchBarn/LWT"
        
      - name: "Barn Entrance Button Signal"
        state_topic: iot/espToggleSwitchBarn/status
        unit_of_measurement: "dB"
        device_class: signal_strength
        availability_topic: "iot/espToggleSwitchBarn/LWT"
        icon: mdi:router-wireless

```

throws the error.
note, I actually have it like this
```
mqtt:
  sensor: !include mqtt_sensor.yaml
```

I still can't reproduce 3), this works fine:
configuration.yaml:
```yaml
mqtt:
  sensor: !include mqtt_sensor.yaml
```

mqtt_sensor.yaml
```yaml
- name: "Barn Entrance Button Clicks"
  state_topic: iot/espToggleSwitchBarn/click
  unit_of_measurement: "click"
  icon: mdi:radiobox-marked
  availability_topic: "iot/espToggleSwitchBarn/LWT"
        
- name: "Barn Entrance Button Signal"
  state_topic: iot/espToggleSwitchBarn/status
  unit_of_measurement: "dB"
  device_class: signal_strength
  availability_topic: "iot/espToggleSwitchBarn/LWT"
  icon: mdi:router-wireless
```

> I still can't reproduce 3), this works fine: configuration.yaml:
> 
> ```yaml
> mqtt:
>   sensor: !include mqtt_sensor.yaml
> ```
> 
> mqtt_sensor.yaml
> 
> ```yaml
> - name: "Barn Entrance Button Clicks"
>   state_topic: iot/espToggleSwitchBarn/click
>   unit_of_measurement: "click"
>   icon: mdi:radiobox-marked
>   availability_topic: "iot/espToggleSwitchBarn/LWT"
>         
> - name: "Barn Entrance Button Signal"
>   state_topic: iot/espToggleSwitchBarn/status
>   unit_of_measurement: "dB"
>   device_class: signal_strength
>   availability_topic: "iot/espToggleSwitchBarn/LWT"
>   icon: mdi:router-wireless
> ```

Very strange. I removed the quotes again, and reloaded, and now it works fine. I guess we can close this :(
Wish we could find what caused that strange hickup.

Maybe has something to do with migrations (so only happens on the first change from old to new syntax)?

**thanks for looking into this so quickly!**
OK, let's forget about 3) for now. Please open a new issue if you manage to reproduce it 👍
